clue.text: Old transporter, truck loaded with embroidered lace

indicators.note: a truck loaded with something carries it inside, so the next letters go into the truck

parts.note: a tipper is a lorry whose body tilts to dump its load

indicators.note: embroidered means worked over and decorated, so the letters of lace are reworked

explanation.surface: A description of an antique wagon heaped with fancy embroidered lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidered' rearranges LACE into EACL, which 'loaded with' sets inside TIPPER, a dumper truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea clipper was a fast nineteenth-century sailing ship carrying tea cargoes from China, so an old transporter.

clue.text: Leading man I suspect, about which a word of caution?

indicators.note: the word of caution sits about, that is around, the scrambled letters

parts.note: "Don't!" is a short warning, written here without its apostrophe

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not reliable, so the letters of man I are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a leading man and wonders what warning to give about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' turns MAN I into MINA, and 'about which' puts DONT round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dominant is in the commanding position, so leading is a synonym in the sense of ruling or foremost.

clue.text: Relish difficult situation

definitions.meaning: a chutney or preserve of vegetables in vinegar eaten as a condiment
a mess or predicament, as in being in a right fix

explanation.surface: Someone savours a tricky predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a vinegar-preserved condiment and, idiomatically, a sticky plight or jam.

clue.text: A cipher featured in news soon

indicators.note: to be featured in something is to appear within it, so the cipher goes inside

parts.note: N is short for new, so news read as plural new things gives two Ns
a cipher is a zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A secret code appears in the news shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' puts O, the zero, between the two Ns that 'news' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: In old or literary English the adverb means shortly, in a little while, a synonym of soon.

clue.text: Tree — positive thing planting 50 x 2

indicators.note: times two, meaning the whole construction is written twice over
the positive thing has 50 planted in it, so that letter goes inside

parts.note: in Chinese thought yang is the positive, active principle, opposite yin
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A gardening note: plant something positive, with fifty of them twice over, to get a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planting' sets L inside YANG to make YLANG, and 'x 2' doubles it. Yang is the Chinese positive principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ylang-ylang is a tropical Asian tree whose fragrant flowers yield an oil used in perfumes.

clue.text: Obvious figure, hidden meaning

parts.note: overt means open and plain to see
one is a number, that is a figure

explanation.surface: A contrast between a plain numeral and a concealed sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets obvious against hidden, but obvious is wordplay and only the second half defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is an implied or subtle additional sense, a connotation lying beneath the stated words.

clue.text: Bird hunter cut loose after evisceration

indicators.note: cut means docked, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: Orion is the great hunter of Greek myth, also a constellation

indicators.note: eviscerating removes the innards, leaving only the outside letters of loose

explanation.surface: A grisly hunting scene: the hunter cuts a bird loose after gutting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks ORION to ORIO; 'after evisceration' empties LOOSE to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orioles are brightly coloured songbirds, often yellow and black, found across Europe and the Americas.

clue.text: Table for a Jamaican fool and poltroon

parts.note: a jerk is a stupid or contemptible person
a poltroon is a coward, informally a chicken

explanation.surface: A Jamaican dining table set for an idiot and a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' means the food served, as in keeping a good table.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerk chicken, chicken marinated in hot spices and grilled, is a classic Jamaican dish, so fare for the Jamaican table.

clue.text: Moving book back, Orwell initially secured by bent nail

indicators.note: back tells us to read the book word in reverse

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: something secured by another is held within it, so the letter is enclosed
a bent nail is out of shape, so its letters are twisted into a new order
initially picks out the opening letter of the author's name

explanation.surface: A book by Orwell is pinned up with a crooked nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives EMOT; 'bent' makes NAIL into INAL, and 'secured by' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving scene stirs the feelings, so it is touching or affecting in that sense.

clue.text: French author puts bird behind geese, flying

indicators.note: the bird is put behind, after, the shape of the flock

parts.note: skeins of geese fly in a V formation
an erne is a sea eagle, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A French writer places a bird at the back of a flight of geese.
explanation.walkthrough: Flying geese form a V shape, which supplies that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne was the French novelist of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

clue.text: See 8
County needing way to avoid country music genre

indicators.note: the country is to avoid the word way, so those letters are dropped from it

parts.note: Norway is a Scandinavian country
taken as written, the word to be removed
folk is a genre of traditional music

explanation.surface: A county seems to need some way of steering clear of country music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' takes WAY out of NORWAY, leaving NOR. Norfolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk is a rural English county on the North Sea coast, an instance of a county.

clue.text: Hook perhaps scratching head, incandescent

indicators.note: scratching out its head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Captain Hook of Peter Pan is an example of a pirate

explanation.surface: Captain Hook scratches his head, burning with rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' strikes the first letter from PIRATE. 'perhaps' signals Hook is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent is used figuratively for someone white-hot with fury, a synonym of very angry.

clue.text: Unknown number it's understood, endless wine bottles for old movie star

indicators.note: to bottle is to contain, so the wine holds the other pieces
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities
Roger is the radio reply meaning message received and understood

explanation.surface: A cryptic recipe: an unknown quantity, some radio jargon and wine bottles add up to a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ROSE to ROS, which 'bottles' wraps round Y and ROGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Rogers was the singing cowboy of Hollywood westerns in the 1940s and 1950s.

clue.text: Those picking up signals there's evidence of wailing in the synagogue?

definitions.meaning: an indoor television aerial with two telescopic antennas in a V shape

definitions.text: evidence of wailing in the synagogue?
definitions.meaning: a Jewish religious leader's tears, the second sense read with a different word break

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at receivers and at weeping heard in a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Re-spaced, the answer reads RABBI TEARS: a rabbi's tears show wailing in the synagogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit ears is the nickname for a two-pronged indoor TV antenna, which picks up broadcast signals.

clue.text: Scores in southern river determined quality

indicators.note: the scores go in, inside, the river

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
to score is to mark with lines, so scores are lines

explanation.surface: Scores of something lie in a river down south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places LINES inside TEES; S comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeliness is hard, unyielding resolve, the quality of a determined person.

clue.text: Keep your chin up to apply warpaint?

definitions.text: Keep your chin up to apply warpaint?

parts.words: Keep your chin up to apply warpaint?
parts.note: the idiom for staying cheerful in adversity, read literally as daubing a bold, fierce look on one's face

explanation.surface: Encouragement to stay cheerful while putting on battle make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Warpaint is a warrior's face paint and slang for make-up, so applying it literally gives a face that looks brave.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide distress behind a cheerful look is to keep one's chin up, and literally warpaint gives a fierce face.

clue.text: Bird which occupies nest until chicks hungry, primarily

indicators.note: to occupy a space is to sit within it, so the pronoun goes inside
primarily means firstly, taking the opening letter of each of the four words

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns

explanation.surface: A bird sits in the nest until the hungry chicks need feeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives NUCH from the starts of nest, until, chicks, hungry, and 'occupies' sets THAT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small woodland songbird that climbs tree trunks head first.

clue.text: Historian head examiner discussed?

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so we take the sound of the word

parts.note: a psychoanalyst examines the mind, so is jokingly one who examines heads

explanation.surface: A historian wonders if the chief examiner has been talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discussed' asks for the sound: ANALYST, a shrink who examines heads.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, year-by-year chronicles, so is a kind of historian.

clue.text: Proper bit of 11 in position

parts.note: right means correct or proper
a wing is a part of a chicken, the answer at 11

explanation.surface: A proper piece of the 11 in place, like a team line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 looks like a football team, but it points to the answer at 11-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Right wing is a playing position on the right flank in football or hockey.

clue.text: What one gets when noticing mixed drink

parts.note: the answer read as a recipe: two named ingredients, stirred together as letters, make the word noticing

explanation.surface: A cocktail is what you are served when someone spots you want a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What one gets when' signals working backwards: GIN and TONIC, mixed, give NOTICING. No clue word supplies the AND, which is why the blog doubts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit topped with quinine water is a classic long drink served with ice and lemon.

clue.text: Ultimate bit of fluff in a leotard

indicators.note: only a bit of the phrase is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A last scrap of fluff caught in a dancer's leotard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' asks for a stretch inside 'fluff in a leotard', crossing the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Final and ultimate are synonyms meaning coming last or at the end.

clue.text: First to fall, in short, a downward distance

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken
short means docked, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A falling object covers a short distance straight down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips AT HOME, the sense of 'in', to ATHOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathom is six feet, the unit for measuring water depth, so a distance downwards.

clue.text: Dance with me for some fiddling

parts.note: the conga is a Latin American line dance

explanation.surface: An invitation to dance, with some fiddle music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' looks musical but means cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: A con game is a swindle; something for fiddling is a means of cheating or defrauding someone.

clue.text: Pretty detached, remote ultimately

parts.note: something cut off has been detached

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone attractive but aloof and distant in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty detached' reads as fairly aloof, but pretty is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means attractive in a charming way, a synonym of pretty.

clue.text: Barcelona's tomboy?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat and a boy can be Alan, so tomboy split up spells out the answer

explanation.surface: A girl in Barcelona who plays rough.
explanation.walkthrough: Tomboy splits into tom (CAT) and a boy's name (ALAN); Barcelona's gives the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is capital of Catalonia, so anything from there is Catalan.

clue.text: Patient enquiry

definitions.meaning: a person under a doctor's care is spoken of as a medical instance
an investigation, as a detective or court looks into a matter

explanation.surface: A doctor's patient query.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors call a patient a case, and a police investigation is also called a case.

clue.text: See 20
Openers: with those for Sussex and Surrey testing reactions

indicators.note: testing hints at Test cricket and at putting letters through trials, so they are rearranged
those refers back to openers, so the opening letters of the two counties

explanation.surface: Cricket: the opening batsmen for Sussex and Surrey test their reflexes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those for' takes the openers, first letters, of Sussex and Surrey; 'testing' scrambles them with OPENERS. Sussex and Surrey are English county cricket sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses are reactions, replies to a stimulus or situation.
